source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
Banana aphid (ចង្រិត) is a small sap-sucking insect that clusters on young leaves and the base of the pseudostem. Its direct feeding damage is minor, but it is the vector that transmits Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV), which is incurable once a plant is infected; infected plants show stunted, narrow, upright leaves bunched at the top ("bunchy top") and never produce a normal bunch.

Because there is no cure for BBTV, management focuses on prevention: controlling the aphid vector with a registered insecticide (the source lists options including imidacloprid, dinotefuran, pymetrozine, acephate, and buprofezin, to be rotated and applied per label), and removing and destroying any plant showing bunchy-top symptoms immediately to stop it from being a source of further aphid-transmitted infection.
